text:
anya: starting a quick ownerless sweep for admin roles (prod + staging). goal: reduce orphaned admin principals and collect audit evidence. target window: 72h, canary first.

mike: 👍 what's the inactivity cutoff? 90 or 120 days? some infra services are seasonal.

jon: i recommend 120d for initial pass to avoid churn. query i'll run in staging: `SELECT principal, role, max(event_time) as last_seen FROM auth_events WHERE role LIKE '%admin%' GROUP BY principal, role HAVING max(event_time) < now() - interval '120 days'`

tori: note — KMS audit logs for projects 18-20 are missing between Jan 15-20 (incidents#245). for those projects we need manual owner attestation before revoking any KMS bindings.

anya: agreed. for projects with log gaps we will attach owner attestation PRs and require 2 approvers from security+platform. put attestation template in the evidence bundle.

liz: prefer canary size ~40 principals across different domains (infra, analytics, ci, infra-service-accounts). run canary, watch 24h, then ramp. no mass removals.

sec-bot: CANARY scheduled 2026-03-26T22:00Z. snapshotting IAM & KMS state, will post diffs to /s3/internal/audit-bundles/3001112223 and alert on any spike in 403/500 from service accounts. :robot_face:

mike: i'll prepare the jq filter for KMS IAM policy extraction: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy $KEY --project=$P --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.role=="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter")'` then cross-ref members with owner tag service.owner=true from our inventory.

jon: i'll assemble candidates CSV: columns = principal, last_seen, roles, suggested_owner, evidence_links. i'll drop screenshots + authlog extracts into the s3 bundle. ETA tomorrow AM.

anya: tasking: mike -> generate canary list + jq filter, jon -> csv + evidence bundle, tori -> owner attestations for KMS-gap projects, liz -> canary execution + rollback playbook, devon -> standby to assist CI/service restores.

devon: what's the explicit rollback mechanism if a job fails post-prune? auto-regrant to a short-lived rescue group or manual support exception? auditors need traceability.

anya: rollback policy: create a ephemeral rescue group `groups/temp-admins/prune-rescue`, grant required roles for 6 hours max via a timestamped grant script; all grants must include a justification and ticket id. we log re-grants to the compliance ticket (RWD-SEC-312).

mike: i'll add an expiry lambda that revokes grants after 6h and writes revocation record. sample command I'll add to runbook: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJ --member='user:$PRINCIPAL' --role='roles/owner' && aws lambda invoke --payload '{"revoke_after":"6h","principal":"$PRINCIPAL","project":"$PROJ"}' revoke-scheduler` (will clean up).

tori: for attestation PRs i'll create a GH template with required fields: owner_email, explanation, approver1, approver2, supporting_log_urls. only merge after 2 approvals.

liz: canary checklist: 1) snapshot current IAM/KMS 2) apply removals for canary list 3) monitor 24h (alerts: 403 spike > +10%, CI failures > 2 new failures) 4) if alerted, run rollback script and open immediate incident.

anya: good. once canary is clean we'll schedule phased removals by team, each with an evidence bundle. keep minimal blast radius.

jon: one more ask — include service-account key last rotation in the CSV so we don't accidentally remove keys used by long-lived jobs. i'll add `sa_key_last_used` column.

anya: perfect. we'll reconvene after jon uploads the bundle. please post the s3 path and the canary diff in this thread. thanks all. :thumbsup:
